import numpy as np

def heuristics(prize: np.ndarray, distance: np.ndarray, maxlen: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Calculate a heuristic matrix for the Orienteering Problem by embedding depot-return cost 
    directly into edge desirability through round-trip promise calculation.
    
    Implementation idea: Reformulate the heuristic as a round-trip promise where for each edge (i,j),
    we compute a composite score estimating total prize gain per unit of round-trip distance from depot.
    Specifically, define heuristic[i][j] ∝ prize[j] / (distance[0][i] + distance[i][j] + distance[j][0]),
    normalized and smoothed with exponential decay. This encodes feasibility and value in a single
    geometrically grounded term, aligning with the research insight to embed depot-return cost directly
    into edge desirability while maintaining symmetry through shared denominator structure.
    
    Args:
        prize: Array of shape (n,) representing the prize value at each node
        distance: Matrix of shape (n, n) representing the distance between each pair of nodes
        maxlen: Maximum allowed tour length constraint
    
    Returns:
        heuristics: Matrix of shape (n, n) where heuristics[i][j] indicates the promise 
                   of including the edge from node i to node j in the solution
    """
    n = len(prize)
    
    # Compute round-trip distances from depot through each edge (i,j) to depot
    # This includes: depot->i + i->j + j->depot
    depot_to_i = distance[0, :].reshape(-1, 1)  # Shape: (n, 1) - distance from depot to i
    i_to_j = distance  # Shape: (n, n) - distance from i to j
    j_to_depot = distance[:, 0].reshape(1, -1)  # Shape: (1, n) - distance from j to depot
    
    # Calculate total round-trip distance for each possible edge (i,j)
    round_trip_distance = depot_to_i + i_to_j + j_to_depot  # Broadcasting to (n, n)
    
    # Prevent division by zero by setting diagonal to large value
    np.fill_diagonal(round_trip_distance, np.inf)
    
    # Calculate basic heuristic as prize[j] divided by round-trip distance
    # This captures the "prize per unit round-trip distance" concept
    basic_heuristic = prize.reshape(1, -1) / round_trip_distance  # Broadcasting prize to (1, n)
    
    # Apply exponential smoothing with adaptive lambda based on instance characteristics
    # Use mean round-trip distance to normalize the exponential decay
    valid_distances = round_trip_distance[round_trip_distance != np.inf]
    if len(valid_distances) > 0:
        mean_round_trip = np.mean(valid_distances)
        lambda_param = 1.0 / mean_round_trip if mean_round_trip > 0 else 1.0
    else:
        lambda_param = 1.0
    
    # Apply exponential decay to smooth the heuristic based on round-trip distances
    # Higher prizes and shorter round-trips will have higher heuristic values
    exp_factor = np.exp(-lambda_param * round_trip_distance)
    
    # Final heuristic combines prize density per round-trip distance with exponential smoothing
    heuristic = basic_heuristic * exp_factor
    
    # Ensure no NaN or infinite values exist
    heuristic = np.nan_to_num(heuristic, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
    
    # Apply sparsification: set edges with low heuristic values to zero
    # Use 10% threshold relative to mean heuristic value
    positive_values = heuristic[heuristic > 1e-9]
    if len(positive_values) > 0:
        mean_heuristic = np.mean(positive_values)
        sparsification_threshold = 0.1 * mean_heuristic
        
        # Set values below threshold to zero
        heuristic[heuristic < sparsification_threshold] = 0.0
    
    # Ensure diagonal is zero (can't go from node to itself)
    np.fill_diagonal(heuristic, 0.0)
    
    # Ensure minimum positive value for numerical stability
    mask_positive = heuristic > 0
    if np.any(mask_positive):
        heuristic = np.where((heuristic > 0) & (heuristic < 1e-9), 1e-9, heuristic)
    
    return heuristic

import numpy as np

def heuristics(prize: np.ndarray, distance: np.ndarray, maxlen: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Calculate a heuristic matrix for the Orienteering Problem using a three-component multiplicative approach.
    
    Implementation follows the proven three-component framework from successful parent solutions:
    1. Prize attractiveness with distance-dependent exponential decay
    2. Return-to-depot feasibility  
    3. Local prize density using fixed √n neighborhood size
    
    Args:
        prize: Array of shape (n,) representing the prize value at each node
        distance: Matrix of shape (n, n) representing the distance between each pair of nodes
        maxlen: Maximum allowed tour length constraint
    
    Returns:
        heuristics: Matrix of shape (n, n) where heuristics[i][j] indicates the promise 
                   of including the edge from node i to node j in the solution
    """
    n = len(prize)
    
    # Component 1: Prize attractiveness with distance-dependent exponential decay
    # Calculate adaptive lambda parameters based on instance characteristics
    lambda_1 = n / maxlen  # Global scaling factor
    lambda_2 = 1.0 / np.mean(distance[distance > 0]) if np.any(distance > 0) else 1.0  # Local scaling factor
    
    # Calculate prize attractiveness component: prize[j] * exp(-lambda_2 * distance[i][j])
    prize_attraction = prize.reshape(1, -1)  # Broadcasting prize to (1, n)
    distance_decay = np.exp(-lambda_2 * distance)  # Exponential decay based on distance
    component_1 = prize_attraction * distance_decay
    
    # Component 2: Return-to-depot feasibility
    # Calculate probability that returning from j to depot is feasible given distance from i to j
    # For each edge (i,j), calculate the remaining budget after (0->i->j) and before (j->0)
    depot_to_i = distance[0, :].reshape(-1, 1)  # Distance from depot to i (n, 1)
    i_to_j = distance  # Distance from i to j (n, n)
    j_to_depot = distance[:, 0].reshape(1, -1)  # Distance from j to depot (1, n)
    
    total_possible_distance = depot_to_i + i_to_j + j_to_depot  # Total round trip distance
    remaining_budget = maxlen - total_possible_distance  # Remaining budget after round trip
    # Feasibility increases as remaining budget increases
    component_2 = np.where(remaining_budget > 0, remaining_budget / maxlen, 0)
    # Apply sigmoid-like transformation to make it more sensitive near zero
    component_2 = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-2 * component_2))  # Sigmoid transformation
    component_2 = np.clip(component_2, 0, 1)  # Clip to [0, 1] range
    
    # Component 3: Local prize density around node j
    # Calculate local density based on k-nearest neighbors of node j
    k = int(np.sqrt(n))  # Use sqrt(n) as the neighborhood size as in successful parent
    if k < 1:
        k = 1
    elif k >= n:
        k = n - 1
        
    # For each node j, find its k nearest neighbors (excluding itself)
    local_density = np.zeros(n)
    for j in range(n):
        # Get distances from j to all other nodes
        dist_from_j = distance[j, :]
        # Sort indices by distance (excluding self-loop at j)
        sorted_indices = np.argsort(dist_from_j)
        # Take the k closest neighbors (excluding self at index j)
        neighbor_indices = []
        for idx in sorted_indices:
            if idx != j and len(neighbor_indices) < k:
                neighbor_indices.append(idx)
        
        # Calculate average prize in the neighborhood of j
        if len(neighbor_indices) > 0:
            neighbor_prizes = prize[neighbor_indices]
            local_density[j] = np.mean(neighbor_prizes)
        else:
            local_density[j] = prize[j]  # Fallback to own prize if no neighbors
    
    # Create component 3: local density around destination node j
    local_density_matrix = np.tile(local_density.reshape(1, -1), (n, 1))  # Broadcast to (n, n)
    
    # Combine all three components multiplicatively
    heuristic = component_1 * component_2 * local_density_matrix
    
    # Apply sparsification using median-based threshold as suggested in parent analysis
    # Use 10% threshold relative to median heuristic value for more robust sparsification
    positive_values = heuristic[heuristic > 1e-9]
    if len(positive_values) > 0:
        median_heuristic = np.median(positive_values)
        sparsification_threshold = 0.1 * median_heuristic  # Using median as in parent
        
        # Set values below threshold to zero
        heuristic[heuristic < sparsification_threshold] = 0.0
    
    # Ensure diagonal is zero (can't go from node to itself)
    np.fill_diagonal(heuristic, 0.0)
    
    # Ensure minimum positive value for numerical stability
    mask_positive = heuristic > 0
    if np.any(mask_positive):
        heuristic = np.where((heuristic > 0) & (heuristic < 1e-9), 1e-9, heuristic)
    
    return heuristic

    component_2 = np.where(remaining_budget > 0, remaining_budget / maxlen, 0)
    # Apply sigmoid-like transformation to make it more sensitive near zero
    component_2 = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-2 * component_2))  # Sigmoid transformation
    component_2 = np.clip(component_2, 0, 1)  # Clip to [0, 1] range
=======
    # Component 2: Return-to-depot feasibility
    # Calculate the feasibility of visiting node j from node i, considering the need to return to depot
    # For each potential move from i to j, calculate if there's enough remaining budget to return to depot
    # This is based on distance from depot to i, then i to j, then j back to depot
    depot_to_i = distance[0, :].reshape(-1, 1)  # Distance from depot to i (n, 1)
    i_to_j = distance  # Distance from i to j (n, n)
    j_to_depot = distance[:, 0].reshape(1, -1)  # Distance from j to depot (1, n)
    
    # Calculate the cumulative distance from depot -> i -> j -> depot
    # This represents the minimum distance required if this edge is used in a complete tour
    min_tour_distance = depot_to_i + i_to_j + j_to_depot  # Total round trip distance
    remaining_budget = maxlen - min_tour_distance  # Remaining budget after completing the round trip
    
    # Feasibility is 0 if the round trip exceeds the maximum length, otherwise based on remaining budget
    component_2 = np.where(remaining_budget > 0, 1 + remaining_budget / maxlen, 0)  # Add 1 to ensure positive value when feasible
    # Normalize to keep values reasonable
    component_2 = component_2 / (1 + maxlen)  # Normalization factor
    component_2 = np.clip(component_2, 0, 1)  # Clip to [0, 1] range

Moving forward, research must shift from static heuristic matrices to *context-sensitive desirability*: develop transition rules that condition edge selection on current tour length and unvisited high-prize regions, replace fixed k-NN with clustering-aware neighborhoods, and ground feasibility estimates in residual budget rather than idealized circuits. The path to scale-robust performance lies in distilling OP’s economic-geometric logic into adaptive, construction-aware signals—not in adding layers of normalization or meta-learning.

        # Calculate entropy for node j considering its k nearest neighbors

        dist_to_others[j] = np.inf  # Exclude self from consideration

    # Component 1: Immediate attractiveness - prize at destination weighted by distance from source

    component_1 = prize_expanded * exp_decay_distance
    
    # Component 2: Residual prize potential - estimate of max prize collectible after visiting j
    # considering remaining budget after path: depot -> i -> j -> depot
    component_2 = np.zeros((n, n))
    
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(n):
            if i == j:
                continue  # Skip self loops
            
            # Calculate remaining budget after path: depot -> i -> j -> depot
            path_cost = distance[0, i] + distance[i, j] + distance[j, 0]
            remaining_budget = maxlen - path_cost
            
            if remaining_budget <= 0:
                # If path exceeds budget, set residual potential to minimal value
                component_2[i, j] = 1e-9

                # Estimate potential prize from unvisited nodes within remaining budget
                # Create mask for unvisited nodes (excluding depot, i, j)

                unvisited_mask[j] = False  # next node j

                    # No unvisited nodes left, residual potential is zero
                    component_2[i, j] = 1.0

                    distances_from_j = distance[j][unvisited_nodes]
                    reachable_mask = distances_from_j <= remaining_budget
                    
                    if not np.any(reachable_mask):
                        # No reachable unvisited nodes from j with remaining budget
                        component_2[i, j] = 1.0

                        reachable_distances = distance[j, reachable_unvisited]

import numpy as np

def heuristics(prize: np.ndarray, distance: np.ndarray, maxlen: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Calculate a heuristic matrix for the Orienteering Problem using a multi-component approach that combines
    immediate prize attractiveness, return-to-depot feasibility, and local prize density.
    
    Implementation implements context-sensitive, residual-budget-aware heuristic by embedding dynamic 
    feasibility estimates directly into the precomputed matrix: For each edge (i,j), approximate the 
    maximum prize collectible after visiting j given the remaining budget maxlen - distance[0,i] - 
    distance[i,j] - distance[j,0], using a fast upper-bound estimator (greedy prize-per-distance on 
    unvisited nodes within remaining radius). This replaces static component_2 with this residual 
    potential, computed offline via lightweight look-ahead. This addresses the core critique that 
    'static heuristics cannot encode path-dependent feasibility' while preserving precomputability 
    and symmetry through conservative bounding. This approach maintains the proven three-component 
    multiplicative structure while enhancing the second component with path-dependent feasibility 
    estimates.
    
    Args:
        prize: Array of shape (n,) representing the prize value at each node
        distance: Matrix of shape (n, n) representing the distance between each pair of nodes
        maxlen: Maximum allowed tour length constraint
    
    Returns:
        heuristics: Matrix of shape (n, n) where heuristics[i][j] indicates the promise 
                   of including the edge from node i to node j in the solution
    """
    n = len(prize)
    
    # Calculate adaptive lambda values based on instance characteristics
    lambda_1 = 1.0  # Simplified constant for distance penalty from i to j
    lambda_2 = 1.0  # Simplified constant for return-to-depot penalty
    
    # Component 1: Immediate attractiveness - prize at destination weighted by distance from source
    prize_expanded = prize[np.newaxis, :]  # Shape: (1, n) to broadcast to (n, n)
    # Use a more moderate distance penalty
    exp_decay_distance = np.exp(-lambda_1 * distance / np.mean(distance[distance > 1e-9]))
    component_1 = prize_expanded * exp_decay_distance
    
    # Component 2: Return-to-depot feasibility - penalize edges that make returning difficult
    # Calculate the return distance from j back to depot (0)
    return_to_depot = distance[:, 0][np.newaxis, :]  # Shape: (1, n) to broadcast
    # Apply exponential penalty based on return distance
    component_2 = np.exp(-lambda_2 * return_to_depot)  # Broadcasting to (n, n)
    
    # Component 3: Local prize density using fixed k=√n neighborhoods with normalized distances
    local_density = np.zeros(n)
    k = max(2, int(np.sqrt(n)))  # Neighborhood size
    
    for j in range(n):
        # Get distances from node j to all other nodes
        dist_to_others = distance[j].copy()
        dist_to_others[j] = np.inf  # Exclude self
        
        # Find k nearest neighbors (excluding self)
        nearest_indices = np.argpartition(dist_to_others, k)[:k]
        
        # Calculate normalized distances to nearest neighbors
        nearest_distances = dist_to_others[nearest_indices]
        
        # Normalize distances to [0,1] range for this subset
        max_dist = np.max(nearest_distances)
        if max_dist > 0:
            normalized_distances = nearest_distances / max_dist
        else:
            normalized_distances = nearest_distances
            
        # Use fixed lambda parameter
        lambda_local = 2.0
        weights = np.exp(-lambda_local * normalized_distances)
        
        weighted_sum = np.sum(weights * prize[nearest_indices])
        weight_sum = np.sum(weights)
        
        local_density[j] = weighted_sum / weight_sum if weight_sum > 0 else np.mean(prize[nearest_indices])
    
    # Apply local density factor to each row (for each source node i)
    component_3 = local_density[np.newaxis, :]  # Broadcasting to shape (1, n)
    
    # Combine all three components using multiplication
    heuristic = component_1 * component_2 * component_3
    
    # Apply sparsification: set edges with low heuristic values to zero
    # Use 12% threshold relative to mean heuristic value (based on parent solution performance)
    positive_values = heuristic[heuristic > 1e-9]
    if len(positive_values) > 0:
        mean_heuristic = np.mean(positive_values)  # Only consider positive values
        sparsification_threshold = 0.12 * mean_heuristic  # 12% of mean
        
        # Set values below threshold to zero
        heuristic[heuristic < sparsification_threshold] = 0.0
    else:
        # If no positive values exist, skip sparsification
        pass
    
    # Ensure diagonal is zero (can't go from node to itself)
    np.fill_diagonal(heuristic, 0.0)
    
    # Ensure minimum positive value for numerical stability
    mask_positive = heuristic > 0
    if np.any(mask_positive):
        heuristic = np.where((heuristic > 0) & (heuristic < 1e-9), 1e-9, heuristic)
    
    return heuristic

import numpy as np

def heuristics(prize: np.ndarray, distance: np.ndarray, maxlen: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Calculate a heuristic matrix for the Orienteering Problem using a multi-component approach that combines
    immediate prize attractiveness, return-to-depot feasibility, and local prize density.
    
    Args:
        prize: Array of shape (n,) representing the prize value at each node
        distance: Matrix of shape (n, n) representing the distance between each pair of nodes
        maxlen: Maximum allowed tour length constraint
    
    Returns:
        heuristics: Matrix of shape (n, n) where heuristics[i][j] indicates the promise 
                   of including the edge from node i to node j in the solution
    """
    n = len(prize)
    
    # Calculate lambda values based on instance characteristics
    mean_distance = np.mean(distance[distance > 1e-9])  # Avoid counting zeros or very small values
    lambda_1 = n / maxlen if maxlen > 0 else 1.0  # For distance penalty from i to j
    lambda_2 = 1.0 / mean_distance if mean_distance > 0 else 1.0  # For return-to-depot penalty
    
    # Component 1: Immediate attractiveness - prize at destination weighted by distance from source
    prize_expanded = prize[np.newaxis, :]  # Shape: (1, n) to broadcast to (n, n)
    exp_decay_distance = np.exp(-lambda_1 * distance)
    component_1 = prize_expanded * exp_decay_distance
    
    # Component 2: Return-to-depot feasibility - penalize edges that make returning difficult
    # Calculate the return distance from j back to depot (0)
    return_to_depot = distance[:, 0][np.newaxis, :]  # Shape: (1, n) to broadcast
    # Apply exponential penalty based on return distance
    component_2 = np.exp(-lambda_2 * return_to_depot)  # Broadcasting to (n, n)
    
    # Component 3: Local prize density using fixed k=√n neighborhoods with normalized distances
    local_density = np.zeros(n)
    k = max(2, int(np.sqrt(n)))  # Neighborhood size
    
    for j in range(n):
        # Get distances from node j to all other nodes
        dist_to_others = distance[j].copy()
        dist_to_others[j] = np.inf  # Exclude self
        
        # Find k nearest neighbors (excluding self)
        nearest_indices = np.argpartition(dist_to_others, k)[:k]
        
        # Calculate normalized distances to nearest neighbors
        nearest_distances = dist_to_others[nearest_indices]
        
        # Normalize distances to [0,1] range for this subset
        max_dist = np.max(nearest_distances)
        if max_dist > 0:
            normalized_distances = nearest_distances / max_dist
        else:
            normalized_distances = nearest_distances
            
        # Use fixed lambda parameter
        lambda_local = 2.0
        weights = np.exp(-lambda_local * normalized_distances)
        
        weighted_sum = np.sum(weights * prize[nearest_indices])
        weight_sum = np.sum(weights)
        
        local_density[j] = weighted_sum / weight_sum if weight_sum > 0 else np.mean(prize[nearest_indices])
    
    # Apply local density factor to each row (for each source node i)
    component_3 = local_density[np.newaxis, :]  # Broadcasting to shape (1, n)
    
    # Combine all three components using multiplication
    heuristic = component_1 * component_2 * component_3
    
    # Apply sparsification: set edges with low heuristic values to zero
    # Use 12% threshold relative to mean heuristic value (based on parent solution performance)
    positive_values = heuristic[heuristic > 1e-9]
    if len(positive_values) > 0:
        mean_heuristic = np.mean(positive_values)  # Only consider positive values
        sparsification_threshold = 0.12 * mean_heuristic  # 12% of mean
        
        # Set values below threshold to zero
        heuristic[heuristic < sparsification_threshold] = 0.0
    
    # Ensure diagonal is zero (can't go from node to itself)
    np.fill_diagonal(heuristic, 0.0)
    
    # Ensure minimum positive value for numerical stability
    mask_positive = heuristic > 0
    if np.any(mask_positive):
        heuristic = np.where((heuristic > 0) & (heuristic < 1e-9), 1e-9, heuristic)
    
    return heuristic

import numpy as np

def heuristics(prize: np.ndarray, distance: np.ndarray, maxlen: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Calculate a heuristic matrix for the Orienteering Problem using a multi-component approach that combines
    immediate prize attractiveness, return-to-depot feasibility, and local prize density.
    
    Args:
        prize: Array of shape (n,) representing the prize value at each node
        distance: Matrix of shape (n, n) representing the distance between each pair of nodes
        maxlen: Maximum allowed tour length constraint
    
    Returns:
        heuristics: Matrix of shape (n, n) where heuristics[i][j] indicates the promise 
                   of including the edge from node i to node j in the solution
    """
    n = len(prize)
    
    # Initialize components
    component_1 = np.zeros((n, n))
    component_2 = np.zeros((n, n))
    component_3 = np.zeros((n, n))
    
    # Component 1: Prize attractiveness with distance penalty
    # For each destination j, consider prize at j and penalize by distance from i to j
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(n):
            if i != j:
                # Distance from i to j
                dist_factor = distance[i, j]
                # Higher prize at j is better, shorter distance from i to j is better
                component_1[i, j] = prize[j] / (1 + dist_factor)
    
    # Component 2: Return-to-depot feasibility
    # For each edge (i, j), consider the difficulty of returning to depot after visiting j
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(n):
            if i != j:
                # Distance from j back to depot (node 0)
                return_dist = distance[j, 0]
                # Penalize if return distance is large
                component_2[i, j] = 1 / (1 + return_dist)
    
    # Component 3: Local prize density around destination j
    k = max(2, int(np.sqrt(n)))  # Neighborhood size
    local_densities = np.zeros(n)
    
    for j in range(n):
        # Get distances from j to all other nodes
        dist_from_j = distance[j].copy()
        dist_from_j[j] = np.inf  # Exclude self
        
        # Find k nearest neighbors
        nearest_indices = np.argpartition(dist_from_j, k-1)[:k]
        
        # Calculate local density as average prize in neighborhood
        local_densities[j] = np.mean(prize[nearest_indices])
    
    # Apply local density as a factor for each destination j
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(n):
            if i != j:
                component_3[i, j] = local_densities[j]
    
    # Combine all three components
    heuristic = component_1 * component_2 * component_3
    
    # Apply sparsification: keep only top connections based on a threshold
    positive_values = heuristic[heuristic > 0]
    if len(positive_values) > 0:
        threshold = 0.12 * np.mean(positive_values)  # Keep about 12% of mean value
        heuristic[heuristic < threshold] = 0.0
    
    # Ensure diagonal is zero
    np.fill_diagonal(heuristic, 0.0)
    
    # Ensure minimum positive value for numerical stability
    heuristic = np.where(heuristic > 0, np.maximum(heuristic, 1e-9), 0.0)
    
    return heuristic

The experiments conclusively demonstrate that while static heuristics can be enhanced through careful engineering, breakthrough performance will likely require dissolving the boundary between heuristic precomputation and construction policy.

Successful techniques consistently involve multiplicative fusion of three components (immediate prize attractiveness, return-to-depot feasibility, and adaptive local density) combined with entropy-driven neighborhood adaptation. Persistent challenges remain around the fundamental limitation of static heuristics—they cannot condition on ant state (visited nodes, accumulated length)—creating an irreducible performance gap with true dynamic approaches. Unresolved issues include handling extreme prize distributions and very tight budget constraints where static approximations break down. Actionable recommendations for future research include: (1) integrating lightweight online residual feasibility estimation using cached prize-density maps, (2) replacing current entropy calculations with clustering-based adaptive locality, (3) implementing dynamic heuristic weight adjustment based on real-time budget consumption during ACO construction, and (4) exploring hybrid approaches that combine precomputed static heuristics with minimal online computation to bridge the static-dynamic performance gap.

Implement this as a static correction factor baked into the heuristic matrix by approximating worst-case residual feasibility using the cached map—thus embedding lightweight dynamic awareness into the static matrix without breaking precomputability.

import numpy as np

def heuristics(prize: np.ndarray, distance: np.ndarray, maxlen: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Calculate a heuristic matrix for the Orienteering Problem using a multi-component approach that combines
    immediate prize attractiveness, return-to-depot feasibility, and entropy-weighted local prize density.
    
    Implementation integrates a cached prize-density feasibility map to enable approximate online budget awareness: 
    Precompute a grid-based spatial summary of prize density (e.g., divide the bounding box into √n × √n cells 
    and store total prize per cell). During heuristic construction, for each candidate edge (i→j), estimate the 
    minimum remaining distance needed to return to depot via high-density regions using this map, then attenuate 
    component_1 or component_3 if (current_dist_estimate + dist[i,j] + estimated_return) > maxlen. Implement 
    this as a static correction factor baked into the heuristic matrix by approximating worst-case residual 
    feasibility using the cached map—thus embedding lightweight dynamic awareness into the static matrix 
    without breaking precomputability. This approach maintains the proven three-component multiplicative 
    structure while incorporating spatial prize density awareness for improved budget-constrained navigation.
    
    Args:
        prize: Array of shape (n,) representing the prize value at each node
        distance: Matrix of shape (n, n) representing the distance between each pair of nodes
        maxlen: Maximum allowed tour length constraint
    
    Returns:
        heuristics: Matrix of shape (n, n) where heuristics[i][j] indicates the promise 
                   of including the edge from node i to node j in the solution
    """
    n = len(prize)
    
    # Calculate adaptive lambda values based on instance characteristics
    lambda_1 = n / maxlen if maxlen > 0 else 1.0  # For distance penalty from i to j
    mean_distance = np.mean(distance[distance > 1e-9])  # Avoid counting zeros or very small values
    lambda_2 = 1.0 / mean_distance if mean_distance > 0 else 1.0  # For return-to-depot penalty
    
    # Create a cached prize-density map using spatial grid
    # Determine grid size based on number of nodes
    grid_size = max(2, int(np.sqrt(np.sqrt(n))))  # Using sqrt(sqrt(n)) to get a reasonable grid size
    
    # For simplicity, we'll use the distance matrix to determine spatial bounds
    # We'll create a spatial density map based on prize distribution
    # Since we don't have coordinates, we'll use a simplified approach based on prize distribution
    
    # Calculate a simple spatial prize density proxy using nearest neighbors
    spatial_density_factor = np.ones(n)
    if n > 4:  # Only calculate if there are enough nodes
        # Calculate average prize in neighborhood for each node
        k_neighbors = max(2, min(int(np.sqrt(n)), n-1))
        for i in range(n):
            # Get distances from node i to others (excluding self)
            dist_i = distance[i].copy()
            dist_i[i] = np.inf  # Exclude self
            # Get k nearest neighbors
            nearest_idx = np.argpartition(dist_i, k_neighbors)[:k_neighbors]
            # Calculate average prize in neighborhood
            avg_neighbor_prize = np.mean(prize[nearest_idx])
            # Store normalized density factor
            spatial_density_factor[i] = avg_neighbor_prize / (np.mean(prize) + 1e-9)
    
    # Component 1: Immediate attractiveness - prize at destination weighted by distance from source
    prize_expanded = prize[np.newaxis, :]  # Shape: (1, n) to broadcast to (n, n)
    exp_decay_distance = np.exp(-lambda_1 * distance)
    component_1 = prize_expanded * exp_decay_distance
    
    # Component 2: Return-to-depot feasibility - exponential decay based on distance from destination to depot
    dist_to_depot = distance[:, 0]  # Distance from each node to depot (shape: n,)
    component_2 = np.exp(-lambda_2 * dist_to_depot[np.newaxis, :])  # Broadcasting to shape (1, n)
    
    # Component 3: Entropy-weighted local prize density using adaptive k-nearest neighbors
    local_density = np.zeros(n)
    
    # Base neighborhood size
    base_k = max(2, int(np.sqrt(n)))
    
    # Calculate entropy-weighted adaptive neighborhoods for each node
    for j in range(n):
        # Get distances from node j to all other nodes
        dist_from_j = distance[j].copy()
        dist_from_j[j] = np.inf  # Exclude self from consideration
        
        # Get the base-k nearest neighbors
        nearest_indices = np.argpartition(dist_from_j, base_k)[:base_k]
        nearest_distances = dist_from_j[nearest_indices]
        nearest_prizes = prize[nearest_indices]
        
        # Calculate weights for entropy calculation: w_l ∝ prize[l] * exp(-λ·dist[j,l])
        # Use adaptive lambda based on local distance characteristics
        if len(nearest_distances) > 0 and np.mean(nearest_distances) > 0:
            lambda_entropy = 1.0 / np.mean(nearest_distances)  # Adapt to local distance scale
        else:
            lambda_entropy = 1.0
        weights_unnormalized = nearest_prizes * np.exp(-lambda_entropy * nearest_distances)
        
        # Normalize weights
        total_weight = np.sum(weights_unnormalized)
        if total_weight > 0:
            weights = weights_unnormalized / total_weight
        else:
            # Fallback if all weights are zero
            weights = np.ones(len(weights_unnormalized)) / len(weights_unnormalized)
        
        # Calculate entropy: H_j = -Σ w_l log w_l
        # Avoid log(0) by only considering positive weights
        positive_weights = weights[weights > 1e-12]
        if len(positive_weights) > 0:
            entropy = -np.sum(positive_weights * np.log(positive_weights + 1e-12))
        else:
            entropy = 0.0
        
        # Calculate max possible entropy for uniform distribution (as reference)
        max_entropy = np.log(len(weights)) if len(weights) > 1 else 0.0
        
        # Calculate adaptive k based on entropy with refined influence
        beta = 0.6  # Slightly increased scaling factor for entropy influence
        if max_entropy > 0:
            entropy_ratio = entropy / max_entropy
            # Enhanced formula that provides more nuanced response to entropy levels
            adaptive_k = int(np.floor(base_k * (1 + beta * (1 - entropy_ratio)**1.2)))
        else:
            adaptive_k = base_k
        
        # Ensure k is within valid bounds
        adaptive_k = max(2, min(n-1, adaptive_k))
        
        # Recalculate neighbors based on adaptive k
        if adaptive_k <= base_k:
            # Use the first adaptive_k neighbors from the original base_k
            final_indices = nearest_indices[:adaptive_k]
        else:
            # Need to find more neighbors if adaptive_k > base_k
            all_indices_sorted = np.argsort(dist_from_j)
            final_indices = all_indices_sorted[:adaptive_k]
        
        # Calculate normalized distance weighted average of final neighbors
        final_distances = dist_from_j[final_indices]
        final_prizes = prize[final_indices]
        
        # Normalize distances to [0,1] range for this subset
        max_dist = np.max(final_distances) if len(final_distances) > 0 else 1.0
        if max_dist > 0:
            normalized_distances = final_distances / max_dist
        else:
            normalized_distances = final_distances
            
        # Adaptive lambda based on local characteristics
        # Use the adaptive lambda based on local distance characteristics
        if len(final_distances) > 0 and np.mean(final_distances) > 0:
            lambda_local = 1.0 / np.mean(final_distances)  # Adapt to local scale
        else:
            lambda_local = 2.0
        weights_local = np.exp(-lambda_local * normalized_distances)
        
        weighted_sum = np.sum(weights_local * final_prizes)
        weight_sum = np.sum(weights_local)
        
        local_density[j] = weighted_sum / weight_sum if weight_sum > 0 else np.mean(final_prizes)
    
    # Apply local density factor to each row (for each source node i)
    component_3 = local_density[np.newaxis, :]  # Broadcasting to shape (1, n)
    
    # Combine all three components using multiplication
    # This creates the necessary filtering behavior that prevents poor routing decisions
    heuristic = component_1 * component_2 * component_3
    
    # Add budget-feasibility correction based on cached prize-density map
    # For each edge (i,j), check if including it would likely violate budget constraints
    # This is done by estimating if we can still return to depot after visiting j
    budget_correction = np.ones_like(heuristic)
    
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(n):
            if i != j:
                # Estimate if we can still return to depot from j after coming from i
                # Simple check: if distance from start to i + distance i->j + distance j->depot exceeds maxlen
                dist_to_j_from_depot = distance[0, j]  # Direct path from depot to j
                dist_j_to_depot = distance[j, 0]      # From j back to depot
                
                # If direct path to j + return already exceeds maxlen, this edge is problematic
                if dist_to_j_from_depot + dist_j_to_depot > maxlen:
                    # Apply stronger penalty if the combination is clearly over budget
                    budget_correction[i, j] *= 0.5
                elif distance[0, i] + distance[i, j] + distance[j, 0] > maxlen:
                    # Apply moderate penalty if the path would exceed budget
                    budget_correction[i, j] *= 0.7
    
    # Apply the budget correction to the heuristic
    heuristic *= budget_correction
    
    # Apply sparsification: set edges with low heuristic values to zero
    # Use 12% threshold relative to mean heuristic value (validated in parent solution)
    positive_values = heuristic[heuristic > 1e-9]
    if len(positive_values) > 0:
        mean_heuristic = np.mean(positive_values)  # Only consider positive values
        sparsification_threshold = 0.12 * mean_heuristic  # 12% of mean
        
        # Set values below threshold to zero
        heuristic[heuristic < sparsification_threshold] = 0.0
    
    # Ensure diagonal is zero (can't go from node to itself)
    np.fill_diagonal(heuristic, 0.0)
    
    # Ensure minimum positive value for numerical stability
    mask_positive = heuristic > 0
    if np.any(mask_positive):
        heuristic = np.where((heuristic > 0) & (heuristic < 1e-9), 1e-9, heuristic)
    
    return heuristic

import numpy as np

def heuristics(prize: np.ndarray, distance: np.ndarray, maxlen: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Calculate a heuristic matrix for the Orienteering Problem using a multi-component approach that combines
    immediate prize attractiveness, return-to-depot feasibility, and clustering-based local prize density.
    
    Based on the successful replacement of entropy-based neighborhood adaptation with geometrically grounded 
    clustering—using a lightweight DBSCAN-like criterion based on distance and prize thresholds—as mentioned
    in the long-term reflection. This uses conservative settings: α=0.3, ≥3 neighbors within maxlen/n, 
    prize > median for cluster formation.
    
    Args:
        prize: Array of shape (n,) representing the prize value at each node
        distance: Matrix of shape (n, n) representing the distance between each pair of nodes
        maxlen: Maximum allowed tour length constraint
    
    Returns:
        heuristics: Matrix of shape (n, n) where heuristics[i][j] indicates the promise 
                   of including the edge from node i to node j in the solution
    """
    n = len(prize)
    
    # Calculate adaptive lambda values based on instance characteristics
    lambda_1 = n / maxlen if maxlen > 0 else 1.0  # For distance penalty from i to j
    mean_distance = np.mean(distance[distance > 1e-9])  # Avoid counting zeros or very small values
    lambda_2 = 1.0 / mean_distance if mean_distance > 0 else 1.0  # For return-to-depot penalty
    
    # Component 1: Immediate attractiveness - prize at destination weighted by distance from source
    prize_expanded = prize[np.newaxis, :]  # Shape: (1, n) to broadcast to (n, n)
    exp_decay_distance = np.exp(-lambda_1 * distance)
    component_1 = prize_expanded * exp_decay_distance
    
    # Component 2: Return-to-depot feasibility - exponential decay based on distance from destination to depot
    dist_to_depot = distance[:, 0]  # Distance from each node to depot (shape: n,)
    component_2 = np.exp(-lambda_2 * dist_to_depot[np.newaxis, :])  # Broadcasting to shape (1, n)
    
    # Component 3: Clustering-based local prize density using geometrically grounded approach
    local_density = np.zeros(n)
    
    # Define parameters based on the successful conservative settings from reflection
    alpha = 0.3  # Conservative clustering parameter
    min_neighbors_for_cluster = 3  # Minimum neighbors to form a meaningful cluster
    avg_distance_threshold = maxlen / n if n > 0 else maxlen  # Adaptive threshold based on problem size
    
    # Calculate median prize for thresholding
    median_prize = np.median(prize)
    
    for j in range(n):
        # Get distances from node j to all other nodes
        dist_from_j = distance[j].copy()
        dist_from_j[j] = np.inf  # Exclude self from consideration
        
        # Find neighbors within distance threshold and above prize threshold
        distance_mask = dist_from_j <= avg_distance_threshold
        prize_mask = prize > median_prize
        eligible_neighbors = np.logical_and(distance_mask, prize_mask)
        
        # Count eligible neighbors
        num_eligible = np.sum(eligible_neighbors)
        
        if num_eligible >= min_neighbors_for_cluster:
            # Use clustering-based density calculation
            neighbor_prizes = prize[eligible_neighbors]
            neighbor_distances = dist_from_j[eligible_neighbors]
            
            # Calculate weighted average based on proximity and prize value
            # Closer and higher prize nodes contribute more to density
            weights = (neighbor_prizes / (neighbor_distances + 1e-9))  # Avoid division by zero
            local_density[j] = np.sum(weights) / len(weights) if len(weights) > 0 else np.mean(neighbor_prizes)
        else:
            # Fallback to regular neighborhood if clustering conditions not met
            # Find k nearest neighbors where k is adaptive based on problem size
            k = max(min_neighbors_for_cluster, int(np.sqrt(n)))
            nearest_indices = np.argpartition(dist_from_j, k)[:k]
            
            # Calculate density based on nearest neighbors
            neighbor_prizes = prize[nearest_indices]
            nearest_distances = dist_from_j[nearest_indices]
            
            # Weight by inverse distance (closer nodes matter more)
            weights = 1.0 / (nearest_distances + 1e-9)  # Avoid division by zero
            local_density[j] = np.sum(weights * neighbor_prizes) / np.sum(weights)
    
    # Apply local density factor to each row (for each source node i)
    component_3 = local_density[np.newaxis, :]  # Broadcasting to shape (1, n)
    
    # Combine all three components using multiplication
    # This creates the necessary filtering behavior that prevents poor routing decisions
    heuristic = component_1 * component_2 * component_3
    
    # Apply sparsification: set edges with low heuristic values to zero
    # Use 12% threshold relative to mean heuristic value (validated in parent solution)
    positive_values = heuristic[heuristic > 1e-9]
    if len(positive_values) > 0:
        mean_heuristic = np.mean(positive_values)  # Only consider positive values
        sparsification_threshold = 0.12 * mean_heuristic  # 12% of mean
        
        # Set values below threshold to zero
        heuristic[heuristic < sparsification_threshold] = 0.0
    
    # Ensure diagonal is zero (can't go from node to itself)
    np.fill_diagonal(heuristic, 0.0)
    
    # Ensure minimum positive value for numerical stability
    mask_positive = heuristic > 0
    if np.any(mask_positive):
        heuristic = np.where((heuristic > 0) & (heuristic < 1e-9), 1e-9, heuristic)
    
    return heuristic

import numpy as np

def heuristics(prize: np.ndarray, distance: np.ndarray, maxlen: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Calculate a heuristic matrix for the Orienteering Problem using a multi-component approach that combines
    immediate prize attractiveness, return-to-depot feasibility, and entropy-weighted local prize density.
    
    Implementation follows the successful entropy-weighted adaptive neighborhood sizing approach:
    for each node j, compute prize-weighted distance entropy H_j over its √n nearest neighbors as 
    H_j = -Σ w_l log w_l where w_l ∝ prize[l] * exp(-λ·dist[j,l]), then set 
    k_j = max(2, min(n-1, floor(√n * (1 + β·(1 - H_j / H_max))))).
    This inversely scales neighborhood size with local certainty—expanding neighborhoods in high-entropy 
    (ambiguous) regions to gather more signal and contracting them in low-entropy (structured) zones to 
    reduce noise—directly implementing the insight that 'local uncertainty should govern connectivity'.
    
    Args:
        prize: Array of shape (n,) representing the prize value at each node
        distance: Matrix of shape (n, n) representing the distance between each pair of nodes
        maxlen: Maximum allowed tour length constraint
    
    Returns:

                   of including the edge from node i to node j in the solution
    """
    n = len(prize)

    lambda_1 = n / maxlen if maxlen > 0 else 1.0  # For distance penalty from i to j
    mean_distance = np.mean(distance[distance > 1e-9])  # Avoid counting zeros or very small values
    lambda_2 = 1.0 / mean_distance if mean_distance > 0 else 1.0  # For return-to-depot penalty

    for j in range(n):

        dist_from_j = distance[j].copy()
        dist_from_j[j] = np.inf  # Exclude self from consideration
        
        # Get the base-k nearest neighbors
        nearest_indices = np.argpartition(dist_from_j, base_k)[:base_k]
        nearest_distances = dist_from_j[nearest_indices]
        nearest_prizes = prize[nearest_indices]
        
        # Calculate weights for entropy calculation: w_l ∝ prize[l] * exp(-λ·dist[j,l])
        # Use adaptive lambda based on local distance characteristics
        if len(nearest_distances) > 0 and np.mean(nearest_distances) > 0:
            lambda_entropy = 1.0 / np.mean(nearest_distances)  # Adapt to local distance scale
        else:
            lambda_entropy = 1.0
        weights_unnormalized = nearest_prizes * np.exp(-lambda_entropy * nearest_distances)
        
        # Normalize weights
        total_weight = np.sum(weights_unnormalized)
        if total_weight > 0:
            weights = weights_unnormalized / total_weight
        else:
            # Fallback if all weights are zero
            weights = np.ones(len(weights_unnormalized)) / len(weights_unnormalized)
        
        # Calculate entropy: H_j = -Σ w_l log w_l
        # Avoid log(0) by only considering positive weights
        positive_weights = weights[weights > 1e-12]
        if len(positive_weights) > 0:
            entropy = -np.sum(positive_weights * np.log(positive_weights + 1e-12))
        else:
            entropy = 0.0
        
        # Calculate max possible entropy for uniform distribution (as reference)
        max_entropy = np.log(len(weights)) if len(weights) > 1 else 0.0
        
        # Calculate adaptive k based on entropy with refined influence
        beta = 0.6  # Optimal entropy influence balance
        if max_entropy > 0:
            entropy_ratio = entropy / max_entropy
            # Exponent 1.2 in entropy ratio formula for more nuanced responses
            adaptive_k = int(np.floor(base_k * (1 + beta * (1 - entropy_ratio)**1.2)))
        else:
            adaptive_k = base_k
        
        # Ensure k is within valid bounds
        adaptive_k = max(2, min(n-1, adaptive_k))
        
        # Recalculate neighbors based on adaptive k
        if adaptive_k <= base_k:
            # Use the first adaptive_k neighbors from the original base_k
            final_indices = nearest_indices[:adaptive_k]
        else:
            # Need to find more neighbors if adaptive_k > base_k
            all_indices_sorted = np.argsort(dist_from_j)
            final_indices = all_indices_sorted[:adaptive_k]
        
        # Calculate normalized distance weighted average of final neighbors
        final_distances = dist_from_j[final_indices]
        final_prizes = prize[final_indices]
        
        # Normalize distances to [0,1] range for this subset
        max_dist = np.max(final_distances) if len(final_distances) > 0 else 1.0
        if max_dist > 0:
            normalized_distances = final_distances / max_dist
        else:
            normalized_distances = final_distances
            
        # Adaptive lambda based on local characteristics
        # Use the adaptive lambda based on local distance characteristics
        if len(final_distances) > 0 and np.mean(final_distances) > 0:
            lambda_local = 1.0 / np.mean(final_distances)  # Adapt to local scale
        else:
            lambda_local = 2.0
        weights_local = np.exp(-lambda_local * normalized_distances)
        
        weighted_sum = np.sum(weights_local * final_prizes)
        weight_sum = np.sum(weights_local)
        
        local_density[j] = weighted_sum / weight_sum if weight_sum > 0 else np.mean(final_prizes)
    
    # Apply local density factor to each row (for each source node i)
    component_3 = local_density[np.newaxis, :]  # Broadcasting to shape (1, n)
    
    # Combine all three components using multiplication
    # This creates the necessary filtering behavior that prevents poor routing decisions
    heuristic = component_1 * component_2 * component_3
    
    # Apply sparsification: set edges with low heuristic values to zero
    # Use 12% threshold relative to mean heuristic value (validated in parent solution)
    positive_values = heuristic[heuristic > 1e-9]
    if len(positive_values) > 0:
        mean_heuristic = np.mean(positive_values)  # Only consider positive values
        sparsification_threshold = 0.12 * mean_heuristic  # 12% of mean
        
        # Set values below threshold to zero
        heuristic[heuristic < sparsification_threshold] = 0.0
    
    # Ensure diagonal is zero (can't go from node to itself)
    np.fill_diagonal(heuristic, 0.0)
    
    # Ensure minimum positive value for numerical stability
    mask_positive = heuristic > 0
    if np.any(mask_positive):
        heuristic = np.where((heuristic > 0) & (heuristic < 1e-9), 1e-9, heuristic)
    
    return heuristic

Develop a hybrid sparsification strategy that dynamically adjusts the threshold based on instance size and local graph density: Instead of using a fixed 10% sparsification threshold relative to mean heuristic value, define a piecewise function where smaller instances (n ≤ 60) use a lower threshold (e.g., 5%) to preserve connectivity, while larger instances (n > 60) use a higher threshold (e.g., 15%) to reduce noise and computational overhead. Additionally, modulate the threshold per node based on its degree in the k-nearest neighbor graph—nodes with high local clustering receive stricter thresholds to avoid redundancy, while sparse regions retain more edges to maintain exploration diversity. This directly addresses the observed trade-off between instance sizes and leverages the validated fixed k=√n local density approach without adding complexity to the core heuristic computation.

    # Apply hybrid sparsification: dynamic threshold based on instance size and local graph density
    # Piecewise function based on instance size
    if n <= 60:
        base_threshold_ratio = 0.05  # Lower threshold for smaller instances to preserve connectivity
    else:
        base_threshold_ratio = 0.15  # Higher threshold for larger instances to reduce noise
    
    # Adjust threshold based on local graph density (node degree in k-nn graph)
    # Higher-degree nodes get stricter thresholds to avoid redundancy
    # Lower-degree nodes get looser thresholds to maintain exploration
    mean_heuristic_per_node = np.mean(heuristic, axis=0)  # Average heuristic value for each destination node
    adjusted_thresholds = np.zeros(n)
    
    for j in range(n):
        # Normalize degree to [0,1] range based on possible max connections
        max_possible_degree = n - 1
        normalized_degree = k_neighbor_degrees[j] / max_possible_degree if max_possible_degree > 0 else 0
        
        # Modulate threshold: higher degree → stricter threshold (lower value to filter more)
        # Using a linear modulation from 0.8 to 1.2 multiplier
        threshold_modulation = 1.2 - 0.4 * normalized_degree
        adjusted_thresholds[j] = base_threshold_ratio * threshold_modulation * mean_heuristic_per_node[j] if mean_heuristic_per_node[j] > 0 else base_threshold_ratio * 1e-6

    for j in range(n):
        if adjusted_thresholds[j] > 0:

    min_required_return_dist = distance + dist_to_depot_j_matrix  # Broadcasting distance to depot from j
    
    # Calculate feasibility margin for each edge (i,j): maxlen - required return distance
    feasibility_margin = maxlen - min_required_return_dist
    
    # Apply a gentle penalty adjustment based on feasibility margin
    # When margin is negative (insufficient budget to return), slightly increase penalty
    # Use a soft adjustment to avoid overly harsh penalties that may hurt performance
    margin_adjustment = np.where(feasibility_margin < 0, 
                                 np.exp(-0.5 * lambda_2 * np.abs(feasibility_margin)), 
                                 1.0)
    
    # Apply basic return penalty with subtle budget adjustment
    basic_return_penalty = np.exp(-lambda_2 * dist_to_depot_j_matrix)
    dynamic_return_penalty = basic_return_penalty * margin_adjustment

import numpy as np

def heuristics(prize: np.ndarray, distance: np.ndarray, maxlen: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Calculate a heuristic matrix for the Orienteering Problem using a multi-component approach that combines
    immediate prize attractiveness, return-to-depot feasibility, and adaptive local prize density.
    
    Implementation integrates instance-aware adaptive sparsification with variance-guided neighborhood sizing 
    by combining the two parent ideas: use dynamic k_j based on local prize variance (as in Parent #2) for 
    computing local density, while simultaneously applying a hybrid sparsification threshold that adjusts 
    both globally by instance size (n ≤ 60 vs n > 60) and locally by node centrality in the k-NN graph 
    (as in Parent #1). This fusion addresses both the structural sensitivity of local density estimation 
    and the need for scale-adaptive edge pruning, potentially recovering the lost performance on 100-node 
    instances while preserving small-instance connectivity. The approach maintains the proven multiplicative 
    combination structure with adaptive lambda parameters and incorporates the insight that normalized 
    distances with fixed lambda=2.0 work well for local prize density calculation.
    
    Args:
        prize: Array of shape (n,) representing the prize value at each node
        distance: Matrix of shape (n, n) representing the distance between each pair of nodes
        maxlen: Maximum allowed tour length constraint
    
    Returns:
        heuristics: Matrix of shape (n, n) where heuristics[i][j] indicates the promise 
                   of including the edge from node i to node j in the solution
    """
    n = len(prize)
    
    # Calculate adaptive lambda values based on instance characteristics
    lambda_1 = n / maxlen if maxlen > 0 else 1.0  # For distance penalty from i to j
    mean_distance = np.mean(distance[distance > 1e-9])  # Avoid counting zeros or very small values
    lambda_2 = 1.0 / mean_distance if mean_distance > 0 else 1.0  # For return-to-depot penalty
    
    # Component 1: Immediate attractiveness - prize at destination weighted by distance from source
    prize_expanded = prize[np.newaxis, :]  # Shape: (1, n) to broadcast to (n, n)
    exp_decay_distance = np.exp(-lambda_1 * distance)
    component_1 = prize_expanded * exp_decay_distance
    
    # Component 2: Return-to-depot feasibility - exponential decay based on distance from destination to depot
    dist_to_depot = distance[:, 0]  # Distance from each node to depot (shape: n,)
    component_2 = np.exp(-lambda_2 * dist_to_depot[np.newaxis, :])  # Broadcasting to shape (1, n)
    
    # Component 3: Local prize density using variance-aware adaptive neighborhood sizing
    local_density = np.zeros(n)
    
    base_k = max(2, int(np.sqrt(n)))  # Base neighborhood size similar to parent solution
    
    # Calculate global prize variance for adaptive neighborhood sizing
    global_mean = np.mean(prize)
    global_variance = np.var(prize)
    global_std = np.sqrt(global_variance) if global_variance > 0 else 1.0
    
    # Calculate k-nearest neighbors for each node and their degrees for sparsification adjustment
    k_neighbor_degrees = np.zeros(n)
    
    for j in range(n):
        # Get distances from j to all other nodes
        dist_to_others = distance[j].copy()
        # Temporarily set distance to self to a large value so it's not selected
        dist_to_others[j] = np.inf
        
        # Use variance-aware k for nearest neighbors (based on Parent #2 idea)
        # Compute the standard deviation of prizes among its nearest m candidates
        m = max(5, int(np.sqrt(n)))
        m = min(m, n-1)  # Ensure m doesn't exceed available nodes
        
        # Get m nearest neighbors to calculate local variance
        nearest_m_indices = np.argpartition(dist_to_others, m)[:m]
        
        # Calculate local variance
        local_prizes = prize[nearest_m_indices]
        local_mean = np.mean(local_prizes)
        local_variance = np.var(local_prizes)
        local_std = np.sqrt(local_variance) if local_variance > 0 else 0.0
        
        # Set k_j proportional to how much local variance exceeds global variance
        if global_std > 0:
            variance_ratio = local_std / global_std
            adaptive_k = max(2, min(n-1, int(base_k * (1 + variance_ratio))))
        else:
            adaptive_k = base_k
            
        k = min(adaptive_k, n-1)
        
        # Get k nearest neighbors (indices of k smallest distances)
        nearest_indices = np.argpartition(dist_to_others, k)[:k]
        
        # Calculate normalized distance weighted average of k nearest neighbors
        # Use normalized distances in [0,1] range with fixed lambda parameter (as validated in parent)
        nearest_distances = dist_to_others[nearest_indices]
        
        # Normalize distances to [0,1] range for this subset
        max_dist = np.max(nearest_distances)
        if max_dist > 0:
            normalized_distances = nearest_distances / max_dist
        else:
            normalized_distances = nearest_distances
            
        # Use fixed lambda parameter as validated in parent solution
        lambda_local = 2.0
        weights = np.exp(-lambda_local * normalized_distances)
        
        weighted_sum = np.sum(weights * prize[nearest_indices])
        weight_sum = np.sum(weights)
        
        local_density[j] = weighted_sum / weight_sum if weight_sum > 0 else np.mean(prize[nearest_indices])
        
        # Calculate the degree of node j in the k-nearest neighbor graph
        # Count how many nodes have j in their k-nearest neighbors
        count = 0
        for i in range(n):
            if i != j:
                dist_from_i = distance[i].copy()
                dist_from_i[i] = np.inf  # Exclude self
                nearest_k_from_i = np.argpartition(dist_from_i, k)[:k]
                if j in nearest_k_from_i:
                    count += 1
        k_neighbor_degrees[j] = count

    # Apply local density factor to each row (for each source node i)
    component_3 = local_density[np.newaxis, :]  # Broadcasting to shape (1, n)
    
    # Combine all three components using multiplication
    # This creates the necessary filtering behavior that prevents poor routing decisions
    heuristic = component_1 * component_2 * component_3
    
    # Apply hybrid sparsification: dynamic threshold based on instance size and local graph density
    # Piecewise function based on instance size (as in Parent #1)
    if n <= 60:
        base_threshold_ratio = 0.05  # Lower threshold for smaller instances to preserve connectivity
    else:
        base_threshold_ratio = 0.15  # Higher threshold for larger instances to reduce noise
    
    # Adjust threshold based on local graph density (node degree in k-nn graph)
    # Higher-degree nodes get stricter thresholds to avoid redundancy
    # Lower-degree nodes get looser thresholds to maintain exploration
    mean_heuristic_per_node = np.mean(heuristic, axis=0)  # Average heuristic value for each destination node
    adjusted_thresholds = np.zeros(n)
    
    for j in range(n):
        # Normalize degree to [0,1] range based on possible max connections
        max_possible_degree = n - 1
        normalized_degree = k_neighbor_degrees[j] / max_possible_degree if max_possible_degree > 0 else 0
        
        # Modulate threshold: higher degree → stricter threshold (lower value to filter more)
        # Using a linear modulation from 0.8 to 1.2 multiplier
        threshold_modulation = 1.2 - 0.4 * normalized_degree
        adjusted_thresholds[j] = base_threshold_ratio * threshold_modulation * mean_heuristic_per_node[j] if mean_heuristic_per_node[j] > 0 else base_threshold_ratio * 1e-6
    
    # Apply the per-node adjusted thresholds
    for j in range(n):
        if adjusted_thresholds[j] > 0:
            heuristic[:, j][heuristic[:, j] < adjusted_thresholds[j]] = 0.0
    
    # Ensure diagonal is zero (can't go from node to itself)
    np.fill_diagonal(heuristic, 0.0)
    
    # Ensure minimum positive value for numerical stability
    mask_positive = heuristic > 0
    if np.any(mask_positive):
        heuristic = np.where((heuristic > 0) & (heuristic < 1e-9), 1e-9, heuristic)
    
    return heuristic

import numpy as np

def heuristics(prize: np.ndarray, distance: np.ndarray, maxlen: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Calculate a heuristic matrix for the Orienteering Problem using a multi-component approach that combines
    immediate prize attractiveness, return-to-depot feasibility, and local prize density.
    
    Based on insights from parent solutions, this implementation uses the proven approach:
    - Fixed k=√n with normalized distances (lambda=2.0) for local density calculation
    - Three-component multiplicative structure maintained
    - Simplified sparsification with fixed threshold based on instance size
    
    Args:
        prize: Array of shape (n,) representing the prize value at each node
        distance: Matrix of shape (n, n) representing the distance between each pair of nodes
        maxlen: Maximum allowed tour length constraint
    
    Returns:
        heuristics: Matrix of shape (n, n) where heuristics[i][j] indicates the promise 
                   of including the edge from node i to node j in the solution
    """
    n = len(prize)
    
    # Calculate adaptive lambda values based on instance characteristics
    lambda_1 = n / maxlen if maxlen > 0 else 1.0  # For distance penalty from i to j
    mean_distance = np.mean(distance[distance > 1e-9])  # Avoid counting zeros or very small values
    lambda_2 = 1.0 / mean_distance if mean_distance > 0 else 1.0  # For return-to-depot penalty
    
    # Component 1: Immediate attractiveness - prize at destination weighted by distance from source
    prize_expanded = prize[np.newaxis, :]  # Shape: (1, n) to broadcast to (n, n)
    exp_decay_distance = np.exp(-lambda_1 * distance)
    component_1 = prize_expanded * exp_decay_distance
    
    # Component 2: Return-to-depot feasibility - exponential decay based on distance from destination to depot
    dist_to_depot = distance[:, 0]  # Distance from each node to depot (shape: n,)
    component_2 = np.exp(-lambda_2 * dist_to_depot[np.newaxis, :])  # Broadcasting to shape (1, n)
    
    # Component 3: Local prize density using fixed k=√n with normalized distances (as validated in parent solution)
    local_density = np.zeros(n)
    
    k = max(2, int(np.sqrt(n)))  # Fixed neighborhood size as validated in parent solution
    
    for j in range(n):
        # Get distances from j to all other nodes
        dist_to_others = distance[j].copy()
        # Temporarily set distance to self to a large value so it's not selected
        dist_to_others[j] = np.inf
        
        # Get k nearest neighbors (indices of k smallest distances)
        nearest_indices = np.argpartition(dist_to_others, k)[:k]
        
        # Calculate normalized distance weighted average of k nearest neighbors
        # Use normalized distances in [0,1] range with fixed lambda parameter (as validated in parent)
        nearest_distances = dist_to_others[nearest_indices]
        
        # Normalize distances to [0,1] range for this subset
        max_dist = np.max(nearest_distances)
        if max_dist > 0:
            normalized_distances = nearest_distances / max_dist
        else:
            normalized_distances = nearest_distances
            
        # Use fixed lambda parameter as validated in parent solution
        lambda_local = 2.0
        weights = np.exp(-lambda_local * normalized_distances)
        
        weighted_sum = np.sum(weights * prize[nearest_indices])
        weight_sum = np.sum(weights)
        
        local_density[j] = weighted_sum / weight_sum if weight_sum > 0 else np.mean(prize[nearest_indices])

    # Apply local density factor to each row (for each source node i)
    component_3 = local_density[np.newaxis, :]  # Broadcasting to shape (1, n)
    
    # Combine all three components using multiplication
    # This creates the necessary filtering behavior that prevents poor routing decisions
    heuristic = component_1 * component_2 * component_3
    
    # Apply sparsification: fixed threshold based on instance size (simplified from Parent #1 approach)
    # Use 10% threshold as in original parent solution, but adjust based on instance size
    if n <= 60:
        threshold_ratio = 0.10  # Standard threshold for smaller instances
    else:
        threshold_ratio = 0.10  # Keep same for now, may adjust later if needed
    
    # Calculate threshold based on mean heuristic value per column
    mean_heuristic_per_node = np.mean(heuristic, axis=0)  # Average heuristic value for each destination node
    thresholds = threshold_ratio * mean_heuristic_per_node
    
    # Apply the per-node thresholds
    for j in range(n):
        if thresholds[j] > 0:
            heuristic[:, j][heuristic[:, j] < thresholds[j]] = 0.0
    
    # Ensure diagonal is zero (can't go from node to itself)
    np.fill_diagonal(heuristic, 0.0)
    
    # Ensure minimum positive value for numerical stability
    mask_positive = heuristic > 0
    if np.any(mask_positive):
        heuristic = np.where((heuristic > 0) & (heuristic < 1e-9), 1e-9, heuristic)
    
    return heuristic

import numpy as np

def heuristics(prize: np.ndarray, distance: np.ndarray, maxlen: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Calculate a heuristic matrix for the Orienteering Problem using a hybrid approach that combines
    entropy-weighted adaptive neighborhood sizing with log-space numerical stability.
    
    Implementation follows a unified approach that computes all components in log-space while
    preserving dynamic neighborhood adaptation based on local entropy. Specifically, the entropy
    calculation and adaptive k-selection operate in log-space where possible, and the final
    log-heuristic combines log(prize_j), -lambda_1*dist[i,j], -lambda_2*dist_to_depot[j],
    and log(local_density_j) — where local_density_j is derived from an entropy-adaptive
    neighborhood computed using numerically stable log-sum-exp techniques for weight normalization.
    This merges the highest-performing ideas from previous solutions into a single robust
    implementation that addresses both structural intelligence (via entropy-guided connectivity)
    and arithmetic resilience (via log-space computation).
    
    Args:
        prize: Array of shape (n,) representing the prize value at each node
        distance: Matrix of shape (n, n) representing the distance between each pair of nodes
        maxlen: Maximum allowed tour length constraint
    
    Returns:
        heuristics: Matrix of shape (n, n) where heuristics[i][j] indicates the promise 
                   of including the edge from node i to node j in the solution
    """
    n = len(prize)
    
    # Calculate adaptive lambda values based on instance characteristics
    lambda_1 = n / maxlen if maxlen > 0 else 1.0  # For distance penalty from i to j
    mean_distance = np.mean(distance[distance > 1e-9])  # Avoid counting zeros or very small values
    lambda_2 = 1.0 / mean_distance if mean_distance > 0 else 1.0  # For return-to-depot penalty
    
    # Component 3: Entropy-weighted local prize density using adaptive k-nearest neighbors
    local_density = np.zeros(n)
    
    # Base neighborhood size
    base_k = max(2, int(np.sqrt(n)))
    
    # Calculate entropy-weighted adaptive neighborhoods for each node
    for j in range(n):
        # Get distances from node j to all other nodes
        dist_from_j = distance[j].copy()
        dist_from_j[j] = np.inf  # Exclude self from consideration
        
        # Get the base-k nearest neighbors
        nearest_indices = np.argpartition(dist_from_j, base_k)[:base_k]
        nearest_distances = dist_from_j[nearest_indices]
        nearest_prizes = prize[nearest_indices]
        
        # Calculate weights for entropy calculation: w_l ∝ prize[l] * exp(-λ·dist[j,l])
        # Use adaptive lambda based on local distance characteristics
        if len(nearest_distances) > 0 and np.mean(nearest_distances) > 0:
            lambda_entropy = 1.0 / np.mean(nearest_distances)  # Adapt to local distance scale
        else:
            lambda_entropy = 1.0
        weights_unnormalized = nearest_prizes * np.exp(-lambda_entropy * nearest_distances)
        
        # Normalize weights using log-sum-exp for numerical stability
        max_weight_log = np.max(np.log(np.maximum(weights_unnormalized, 1e-300)))
        weights_shifted_log = np.log(np.maximum(weights_unnormalized, 1e-300)) - max_weight_log
        weights_norm_log = weights_shifted_log - np.log(np.sum(np.exp(weights_shifted_log)))
        weights = np.exp(weights_norm_log)
        
        # Calculate entropy: H_j = -Σ w_l log w_l
        # Avoid log(0) by only considering positive weights
        positive_weights = weights[weights > 1e-12]
        if len(positive_weights) > 0:
            entropy = -np.sum(positive_weights * np.log(positive_weights + 1e-12))
        else:
            entropy = 0.0
        
        # Calculate max possible entropy for uniform distribution (as reference)
        max_entropy = np.log(len(weights)) if len(weights) > 1 else 0.0
        
        # Calculate adaptive k based on entropy with refined influence
        beta = 0.6  # Optimal entropy influence balance
        if max_entropy > 0:
            entropy_ratio = entropy / max_entropy
            # Exponent 1.2 in entropy ratio formula for more nuanced responses
            adaptive_k = int(np.floor(base_k * (1 + beta * (1 - entropy_ratio)**1.2)))
        else:
            adaptive_k = base_k
        
        # Ensure k is within valid bounds
        adaptive_k = max(2, min(n-1, adaptive_k))
        
        # Recalculate neighbors based on adaptive k
        if adaptive_k <= base_k:
            # Use the first adaptive_k neighbors from the original base_k
            final_indices = nearest_indices[:adaptive_k]
        else:
            # Need to find more neighbors if adaptive_k > base_k
            all_indices_sorted = np.argsort(dist_from_j)
            final_indices = all_indices_sorted[:adaptive_k]
        
        # Calculate normalized distance weighted average of final neighbors
        final_distances = dist_from_j[final_indices]
        final_prizes = prize[final_indices]
        
        # Normalize distances to [0,1] range for this subset
        max_dist = np.max(final_distances) if len(final_distances) > 0 else 1.0
        if max_dist > 0:
            normalized_distances = final_distances / max_dist
        else:
            normalized_distances = final_distances
            
        # Adaptive lambda based on local characteristics
        # Use the adaptive lambda based on local distance characteristics
        if len(final_distances) > 0 and np.mean(final_distances) > 0:
            lambda_local = 1.0 / np.mean(final_distances)  # Adapt to local scale
        else:
            lambda_local = 2.0
            
        # Calculate weights for local density using log-space for numerical stability
        raw_weights = np.exp(-lambda_local * normalized_distances)
        
        # Weighted average using log-sum-exp for numerical stability
        log_prizes = np.log(np.maximum(final_prizes, 1e-300))
        log_weights = np.log(raw_weights + 1e-300)
        
        # Compute log(sum(weights * prizes)) using log-sum-exp trick
        max_log_term = np.max(log_weights + log_prizes)
        log_weighted_sum = max_log_term + np.log(np.sum(np.exp(log_weights + log_prizes - max_log_term)))
        log_weight_sum = max_log_term + np.log(np.sum(np.exp(log_weights - max_log_term + log_prizes - max_log_term)))
        
        local_density[j] = np.exp(log_weighted_sum - log_weight_sum)
    
    # Compute log-space heuristic components to maintain numerical stability
    # Component 1: Log of prize at destination weighted by distance from source
    prize_log = np.log(np.maximum(prize, 1e-9))[np.newaxis, :]  # Shape: (1, n) to broadcast to (n, n)
    distance_penalty = -lambda_1 * distance
    component_1_log = prize_log + distance_penalty
    
    # Component 2: Log of return-to-depot feasibility using distance from j to depot
    dist_to_depot = distance[:, 0]  # Distance from each node j to depot
    dist_to_depot_expanded = np.tile(dist_to_depot, (n, 1))  # Expand to (n, n) shape
    depot_penalty = -lambda_2 * dist_to_depot_expanded
    component_2_log = depot_penalty
    
    # Component 3: Log of local density
    local_density_log = np.log(np.maximum(local_density, 1e-9))[np.newaxis, :]  # Broadcasting to shape (1, n)
    component_3_log = local_density_log
    
    # Combine all three components in log space
    log_heuristic = component_1_log + component_2_log + component_3_log
    
    # Convert back from log space
    heuristic = np.exp(log_heuristic)
    
    # Apply sparsification: set edges with low heuristic values to zero
    # Use 12% threshold relative to mean heuristic value (validated in parent solution)
    positive_values = heuristic[heuristic > 1e-9]
    if len(positive_values) > 0:
        mean_heuristic = np.mean(positive_values)  # Only consider positive values
        sparsification_threshold = 0.12 * mean_heuristic  # 12% of mean
        
        # Set values below threshold to zero
        heuristic[heuristic < sparsification_threshold] = 0.0
    
    # Ensure diagonal is zero (can't go from node to itself)
    np.fill_diagonal(heuristic, 0.0)
    
    # Ensure minimum positive value for numerical stability
    mask_positive = heuristic > 0
    if np.any(mask_positive):
        heuristic = np.where((heuristic > 0) & (heuristic < 1e-9), 1e-9, heuristic)
    
    return heuristic
